I'm a huge fan of DRG and rogue-like games, but I don't like this DRG themed rogue-like.

Overall, I don't enjoy this game in its current state for three main reasons.

1. It's a uninteresting and slow rogue-like. Many of the upgrades you can get are flat-stat increases that don't meaningfully change how you customize your character over a course of a run. For example, a flat +20 hp or +12 armor. There are way more of these boring stat increases than the interesting upgrades. These boring stat increases upgrades persist from common to epic upgrades, and often times you come across the same stat increase upgrade, but just in a different rarity. For instance, sometimes I like picking the common-level increased blood sugar percentage gain for a little bit of extra healing in the long run, but it's boring to see the same upgrade AGAIN in my next common upgrade pool or in my higher rarity level pool with increased stats. 

The slow aspect comes from that the characters besides like one (Slasher, maybe Retcon) have no real mobility. You're just stuck running around at base speed, and when you're on a time crunch, it gets pretty stressful and tedious when you're slowly running through a long, connecting tunnel between rooms trying to get to the next major chamber. There are perks that increase your speed like the upgrade that increases base speed with more armor you have or the one that gives you a double jump, but I have only gotten that once in my 20 hours of playing this so far. 

2. RNG of equipment spawns can really screw you over. I remember clearing an entire level with only one ammo pod spawn, and that's the guaranteed one you get at the starting elevator. Sometimes I'm stuck with a common rarity pistols for 2-3 levels because the workbenches aren't feeling generous in giving decent weapons.

3. A lot of the enemies are not fun to fight. Tick bombs that immediately explode and strip all your armor away are super annoying when they crawl around a cliff or corner, leaving you hardly any time to respond. Their audio cues tend to be on the quieter side comparatively to other enemies. A lot of games has a slight timer before explosion enemies explode to balance out the heavy punishment that they can inflict on you. Clamorhead's laser attack don't have an audio cue and can wall bang you. Edgestalkers are incredibly annoying to deal with since they actively run away from you in order to long-distance snipe you. If you're stuck with a common-rarity short range weapon for two-three levels straight and you have no mobility to chase several of these guys down in a rogue spawn event, chasing these guys becomes incredibly un-fun.
